73	### 2. Log a shot
74	
75	1. Today shows the current bag and a "Pull again" button with the last recipe ("18.0 → 36.4 g · grind 11").
76	2. "Pull again" opens the shot form prefilled from the last shot of this bag (or of this coffee, if the bag is
77	   new): dose, yield, grind, water temp, grinder, basket, brew method, milk drink. Time is not prefilled: it starts
78	   as "Not timed · last 29 s", because a copied time would be saved as if it were measured. The grind field shows
79	   the last shot's grind and nothing else; the app doesn't suggest a different one.
80	3. Adjust what changed with steppers (dose and yield in 0.1 g, time in 1 s, grind in the grinder's own step size).
81	   Time has two ways in, both always available: the built-in timer (Start when the pump starts, Stop when it
82	   stops) or typing it. "Type" opens a numeric keypad; tapping any numeral does the same for that field.
83	4. Pick taste (sour, balanced, bitter) and rating (1 to 5). Both start empty; they are the only new information in
84	   a repeat shot. A "Same as last" chip above them ("Same as last: balanced, 4") fills both in one tap when the shot
85	   tasted like yesterday's.
86	5. "Save shot". The saved screen shows the ratio, the time against the 25 to 32 s window, the taste, the shot's
87	   place on the dial-in target among this bag's shots, and one line comparing it with the last shot ("Inside the
88	   window, two seconds slower than Monday's shot"; "Ran fast at 22 s, outside the window"). It describes what
89	   happened and doesn't say what to change. "Undo" stays for 5 s. Undo writes a retraction record (`deleted: true`), not a delete.
90	
91	Repeat shot that tasted the same: Pull again, Start, Stop, "Same as last", Save. Three taps plus the timer. If the
92	taste or rating differs, it's taste and rating instead of "Same as last": four taps plus the timer. Saving without
93	a time turns the button into "Save with 29 s?". A second tap saves the last shot's time, recorded as copied
94	(`time_source` = `copied`), so it never passes for a measured time and the dial-in model leaves it out.

97	
98	From Today or from a bag in the history list: the coffee page. Header with the bag photo, roaster and coffee name,

It never blocks anything. #### Undo strip `--panel`, radius 8, no border: "Shot saved" and an accent "Undo", with a thin line under Undo that shrinks over 5 s. Undo writes a retraction record. #### Edit bag An accent "Edit bag" text link (56 px tall, ending on the gutter) after the roast line on Today and on the coffee page. The form: roaster and coffee, roast date, weight, and "Still using it" / "Finished". Saving writes a new record under the same id (the shots stay with it) and returns to the screen it was opened from, with a notice. A roast date in the future isn't saved; one more than 90 days old asks "Save with day N?". #### Notice What the last save did, at the top of the screen it lands on: "Bag saved: Onyx Geometry", "DF64 V2 saved", "Correction saved", "Shot undone", "Password changed". `--panel`, radius 8, like the Undo strip; `role="status"`, so it's read out (shown empty, then filled, so screen readers announce it). A save queued offline says so: "Saved on this phone. It’ll sync when you’re back online."; a bag names itself, since Today may still show the last one until it syncs: "Bag saved on this phone: Onyx Geometry. It’ll sync when you’re back online." Logging a shot keeps Saved as its confirmation, with Undo. Every save leaves its form: it returns to the screen the form was opened from (Setup, first run, the gear picker on Log shot), stepping back in history, or else replaces the form, so Back never reopens what was just saved. - Bluetooth scales and machine integrations (Acaia, Decent, Gaggiuino). Chrome on Android does support Web Bluetooth, so a scale is possible later; for now typing two numbers is fine. - Pour-over and filter recipes beyond what `brew_method` already stores. The UI is espresso-first. - A reference per drink type. Lungo, Lance Hedrick's "soup" shot and pour-over such as V60 may later get their own; for now there's one window. - Editing or deleting lake files. Corrections and retractions stay new records. - Buying coffee. The coffee page links to the roaster's product page and stops there. - Replacing the MCP server or the issue form. They keep working and gain the new fields where it's cheap. ## User flows ### 1. Capture a bag 1. Today screen → "New bag". The camera opens (a file input with `capture="environment"`, which opens Android's camera without the app asking for camera permission). 2. Take the photo. The phone downsizes it to about 1600 px on the long edge and removes EXIF (GPS included) before upload. 3. The server sends the image to Claude with a fixed JSON schema: `roaster`, `coffee_name`, `roast_date`, `origin`, `process`, `weight_g`, plus a confidence per field. A typical read takes 2 to 5 s; the screen shows a skeleton of the match card meanwhile. 4. The server matches roaster first (against `dim_roaster` names and domains), then the coffee within that roaster's catalog, using `shots.fuzzy_match_coffee`'s scorer. Listed coffees rank above delisted ones. 5. A confident match uses the rule `shots.log_shot` already applies: the top score is at least 80 and at least 5 ahead of the next one. The match card then shows the catalog title, roaster, origin, process, tasting notes, price per 100 g and stock, and the roast date that was read ("Oct 18 · day 9"). It shows no score; the number would only be noise when the answer is clear. 6. One tap on "Use this coffee" writes a `bags` record and opens the shot form. "Pick another match" opens the same list as a weak match. 7. A weak match (below 80, or two candidates within 5 points) skips the card. The sheet asks "Which one is it?", says what was read from the bag, and lists up to three candidates as rows, each with its score ("match 68") so the owner can see how close they are. Tapping a row picks it. "None of these: type the coffee" opens search; if nothing matches (a café bag, a roaster not in the registry), the bag is saved with free text, the same way `coffee_freetext` works today. 8. If the roast date couldn't be read, a date picker defaults to 7 days ago. Two taps when the match is confident, three when it's weak. The bag becomes the "current bag" until another one is started or it's marked finished. ### 2. Log a shot 1. Today shows the current bag and a "Pull again" button with the last recipe ("18.0 → 36.4 g · grind 11").

def jpeg(w=3000, h=2000, exif: bool = True, orientation: int | None = None, fmt="JPEG") -> bytes:
    im = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), (120, 80, 40))
    ex = Image.Exif()
    if exif:
        ex[0x8825] = {2: (37.0, 46.0, 30.0), 1: "N"}  # GPS IFD: a location
        ex[0x010F] = "PhoneMaker"
    if orientation:
        ex[0x0112] = orientation
    out = io.BytesIO()
    im.save(out, fmt, exif=ex.tobytes() if fmt == "JPEG" else None)
    return out.getvalue()


# --- photos --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_photo_is_downsized_and_loses_its_metadata():
    p = photos.normalize(jpeg())
    with Image.open(io.BytesIO(p.jpeg)) as im:
        assert max(im.size) == 1600 and im.format == "JPEG"
        assert not im.getexif() and "exif" not in im.info and "icc_profile" not in im.info
    assert len(p.sha256) == 64 and (p.width, p.height) == (1600, 1067)


def test_photo_is_turned_upright_before_the_orientation_tag_goes():
    p = photos.normalize(jpeg(1200, 800, orientation=6))  # 6: rotate 90°
    assert (p.width, p.height) == (800, 1200)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("data", [b"", b"not an image at all", b"GIF89a" + b"\0" * 64])
def test_bad_uploads_are_refused(data):
    with pytest.raises(photos.BadPhoto):
        photos.normalize(data)


def test_other_image_formats_are_refused():
    out = io.BytesIO()
    Image.new("RGB", (10, 10)).save(out, "GIF")
    with pytest.raises(photos.BadPhoto, match="JPEG, PNG or WebP"):
        photos.normalize(out.getvalue())


def test_huge_pixel_counts_are_refused(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(photos, "MAX_PIXELS", 1000)
    with pytest.raises(photos.BadPhoto):
        photos.normalize(jpeg(100, 100))

in the future isn't saved; one more than 90 days old asks "Save with day N?".

#### Finish bag

A secondary "Finish bag" button at the foot of the coffee page of a bag still in use. One tap writes a new record of
the bag with today's date as `finished_on` (like a retraction, never a delete) and reloads the page with the notice
"Bag finished: Onyx Geometry", where the roast line now ends "finished Oct 31" and the button is gone. A finished
bag leaves Today and the bag pickers (Switch coffee, the bag list when correcting a shot) and stays in Coffees,
marked finished. Offline it waits in the outbox like any other write. Edit bag's "Still using it" puts it back.

def test_undo_writes_a_retraction(client, lake):
    client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W)
    r = client.post("/api/shots/s1/retract", headers=W)  # within the same second as the save
    assert r.json() == {"shot_id": "s1", "written": True}
    assert client.post("/api/shots/s1/retract", headers=W).json()["written"] is False
    assert len(files(lake, "shots")) == 2  # the shot and its retraction; nothing deleted
    assert shots.load_shots(lake) == []
    assert client.get("/saved/s1").status_code == 404
    assert "No shots of this bag yet" in client.get("/").text


def test_cache_is_seeded_from_the_lake(client, lake, monkeypatch):
    old_shot(lake, "old1", "2026-10-20", coffee_freetext="Onyx Geometry", grinder_setting=14.0)
    client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W)
    client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(2), headers=W)
    client.post("/api/shots/s2/retract", headers=W)
    store = create_app(lake, HeaderAuth()).state.store  # a restart
    assert [s.shot_id for s in store.shots_of("owner")] == ["old1", "s1"]  # old shots are the owner's
    assert store.current_bag("owner").bag_id == "bag1"
    assert [e.name for e in store.equipment_of("owner", "grinder")] == ["DF64 V2"]
    # And it's updated on every write, without reading the lake again.
    monkeypatch.setattr(Lake, "latest", lambda *a: pytest.fail("read the lake again"))
    client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(3), headers=W)
    assert [s.shot_id for s in client.app.state.store.shots_of("owner")] == ["s1", "s3"]


def test_users_see_and_change_only_their_own(client, lake):
    bob = W | {"x-test-user": "bob", "X-Expected-User": "bob"}
    client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W)
    assert client.post("/api/shots/s1/retract", headers=bob).status_code == 404
    assert client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1, rating=1), headers=bob).status_code == 404  # no takeover

input.content: """Finish bag: the button on the bag's page writes a new record with finished_on (like a retraction, never a delete); the bag leaves Today and the bag pickers on Today and Log shot, and stays in Coffees.""" from datetime import date, timedelta import pyarrow.parquet as pq from app.main import create_app from .test_app import W, HeaderAuth, client, files, prefill, shot # noqa: F401 - client is a fixture FINISH = {"finished_on": "2026-10-30"} def snapshot(lake, table: str) -> dict: """Every file of a table and its bytes, to show nothing already written was changed or removed.""" return {p.name: p.read_bytes() for p in files(lake, table)} def test_the_bag_page_has_a_finish_button_until_the_bag_is_finished(client): page = client.get("/coffee/bag1").text assert 'data-finish-bag="bag1"' in page and ">Finish bag" in page assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W).status_code == 200 page = client.get("/coffee/bag1").text assert client.get("/coffee/bag1").status_code == 200 assert "data-finish-bag" not in page assert "Roasted Oct 18 · day 12 · finished Oct 30" in page def test_finishing_appends_one_record_and_deletes_nothing(client, lake): client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W) bags_before, shots_before = snapshot(lake, "bags"), snapshot(lake, "shots") r = client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) assert r.json() == {"bag_id": "bag1", "written": True} bags_after = snapshot(lake, "bags") assert {k: v for k, v in bags_after.items() if k in bags_before} == bags_before # untouched new = [lake.root / "bags" / name for name in bags_after.keys() - bags_before.keys()] assert len(new) == 1 (row,) = pq.read_table(new[0]).to_pylist() assert row["bag_id"] == "bag1" and row["finished_on"] == date(2026, 10, 30) and row["deleted"] is False assert (row["coffee_freetext"], row["roast_date"]) == ("Onyx Geometry", date(2026, 10, 18)) # the rest kept assert snapshot(lake, "shots") == shots_before # its shots stay as they were # Finishing again (the outbox resending, a second tap) writes nothing. assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W).json()["written"] is False assert len(files(lake, "bags")) == len(bags_after) # A restart reads it back from the lake: still finished, nothing on the grinder. store = create_app(lake, HeaderAuth()).state.store assert store.bag("owner", "bag1").finished_on == date(2026, 10, 30) assert store.current_bag("owner") is None def test_a_finished_bag_leaves_today(client): client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W) client.post("/api/bags", json={"bag_id": "bag2", "coffee_freetext": "Other coffee"}, headers=W) client.get("/bag/bag2/use") today = client.get("/").text assert "Other coffee" in today and "Switch coffee" in today client.post("/api/bags/bag2/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) today = client.get("/").text # the cookie still names bag2 assert "Other coffee" not in today and "/bag/bag2/edit" not in today assert 'href="/coffee/bag1">Onyx Geometry' in today # the open bag is on the grinder again assert "Switch coffee" not in today # one open bag left: nothing to switch to # The last open bag finished: Today no longer offers it as the bag on the grinder. client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) today = client.get("/").text assert "On the grinder" not in today and 'href="/coffee/bag1"' not in today and "Edit bag" not in today assert prefill(client)["bag_id"] is None # Log shot doesn't put a new shot in it def test_a_finished_bag_leaves_the_bag_pickers(client): client.post("/api/bags", json={"bag_id": "bag2", "coffee_freetext": "Other coffee"}, headers=W) client.post("/api/bags", json={"bag_id": "bag3", "coffee_freetext": "Third coffee"}, headers=W) client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1, bag_id="bag3"), headers=W) assert 'href="/bag/bag2/use"' in client.get("/bags/switch").text assert 'href="/log?correct=s1&bag=bag2"' in client.get("/log?correct=s1").text client.post("/api/bags/bag2/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) switch = client.get("/bags/switch").text assert "/bag/bag2/use" not in switch and "Other coffee" not in switch assert 'href="/bag/bag1/use"' in switch and 'href="/bag/bag3/use"' in switch log = client.get("/log?correct=s1").text # the bag list on Log shot when correcting a shot assert "bag=bag2" not in log and 'href="/log?correct=s1&bag=bag1"' in log assert client.get("/bag/bag2/use").status_code == 404 # nor can it be picked by its link def test_a_finished_bag_still_shows_in_coffees(client): client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W) client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) coffees = client.get("/coffees").text assert 'href="/coffee/bag1"' in coffees and "Onyx Geometry" in coffees assert "1 shot · best rated 4, Oct 21 · finished" in coffees assert "Onyx Geometry" in client.get("/history").text assert client.get("/shot/s1").status_code == 200 def test_finish_is_refused_for_someone_elses_or_a_missing_bag_and_a_bad_date(client, lake): maya = W | {"x-test-user": "maya", "X-Expected-User": "maya"} before = len(files(lake, "bags")) assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=maya).status_code == 404 assert client.post("/api/bags/nope/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W).status_code == 404 future = (date.today() + timedelta(days=5)).isoformat() assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json={"finished_on": future}, headers=W).status_code == 422 assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json={"finished_on": "soon"}, headers=W).status_code == 422 assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH).status_code == 403 # a write needs the app's header assert len(files(lake, "bags")) == before assert client.app.state.store.bag("owner", "bag1").finished_on is None def test_finish_without_a_date_uses_today(client): assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json={}, headers=W).json()["written"] is True assert client.app.state.store.bag("owner", "bag1").finished_on == date.today()

summary:
The bag page now has a "Finish bag" button, committed locally as one commit on `finish-bag`. The full test suite passes; nothing was pushed and no PR was opened.

**Worktree:** `/tmp/co-r3/clones/build-finish-bag-screen-with_skill-2-finish-bag`, branch `finish-bag` from main@6bda240.
**Commit:** `5eb5cb9` "Add a Finish bag button to the bag page"
**Brief:** saved verbatim to `/tmp/co-r3/clones/build-finish-bag-screen-with_skill-2/outputs/04-brief-implementer.md` and not git-added.

**The user's premise is partly wrong.** The app already had a way to finish a bag: the Edit bag form has a "Still using it" / "Finished" toggle, and Today, Switch coffee and Log shot already left out finished bags. What was missing was a Finish action on the bag page itself, so that is what I built. The screens' existing filtering did the rest.

**What changed:**
- **Button:** `app/templates/coffee.html` shows "Finish bag" at the foot of the page for a bag still in use, and hides it once the bag is finished.
- **Record:** pressing it calls a new `POST /api/bags/{bag_id}/finish`, which goes to `Store.finish_bag` in `app/store.py`. It writes a new bags record under the same id with `finished_on` set, the same way retract does: nothing is deleted and no existing lake file is edited.
  - Finishing an already-finished bag writes nothing, so a resend or double tap is harmless.
  - A future date or a malformed date is refused with 422; another person's bag or a missing one gets 404.
  - The date comes from the phone; if none is sent, the server uses today.
- **Phone side:** `app/static/app.js` sends it through the existing offline queue (`finish:` entries, with a "Finishing a bag" label in the failed list). Once delivered, it clears the phone's selected bag if it was this one and drops the saved copies of Today and Log shot. The page reloads with the notice "Bag finished: <name>", and the roast line ends "· finished Oct 31".
- **Docs:** a short "Finish bag" entry in `docs/app/DESIGN.md`.
- **Tests:** a new file, `tests/test_finish_bag.py`, with 7 tests:
  - the button shows, then goes away once finished;
  - exactly one new bags file is written, existing bags and shots files are byte-for-byte unchanged, and a restart reads the bag back as finished;
  - it leaves Today, falling back to the other open bag, or to no current bag;
  - it leaves the Switch coffee picker and the bag list on Log shot, and `/bag/{id}/use` returns 404;
  - it still shows in Coffees marked finished, and in History;
  - the refusal cases above;
  - a finish with no date uses today.

**Tests:**
- Command: `uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -rs` in the worktree.
- Result: `645 passed, 3 skipped, 1 warning in 971.05s (0:16:11)`, exit 0.
- The skips:
  - `test_app_browser.py`: "Node with Playwright not installed" (axe-core is missing).
  - `test_wholesale_accuracy.py` ×2: "WHOLESALE_EVAL_DIR not set".
- The warning is an existing `DecompressionBombWarning` in `test_m4_fixes`.
- The pre-commit hooks (ruff, ruff format, mypy and the rest) pass on the changed files.

**Checked by hand:** I drove the button in headless Chromium against a local app at phone width, using a throwaway script in `/tmp/finishcheck`, outside the repo. It showed the notice, hid the button, Today switched to the other bag with "Switch coffee" gone, Coffees showed "· finished", and there were no JS errors. Before and after screenshots are in `/tmp/finishcheck/`.

**Left out or not done:**
- Un-finishing and deletes, as instructed. Edit bag's existing "Still using it" toggle can still re-open a bag; I didn't change it.
- I didn't change how retract works, and no dbt or model changes were needed.
- No browser test was added to `tests/browser/app_flow.js`: that suite is skipped here, so a new step couldn't be verified.
- The button has no confirmation step or Undo strip; one tap finishes the bag.
- When the last open bag is finished and shots exist, Today shows that coffee's last shot under "Last coffee". This is how Today already behaves with no open bag. The bag isn't on the grinder, and new shots aren't filed under it.
- I didn't get a full-suite run on unmodified main: I stopped that baseline run because I had started editing in the same worktree while it ran.

content.content: """Finish bag: the button on the bag's page writes a new record with finished_on (like a retraction, never a delete); the bag leaves Today and the bag pickers on Today and Log shot, and stays in Coffees.""" from datetime import date, timedelta import pyarrow.parquet as pq import pytest from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from app.main import create_app from .test_app import HeaderAuth, W, files, prefill, setup, shot FINISH = {"finished_on": "2026-10-30"} @pytest.fixture def client(lake): """Equipment and one open bag, bag1 (Onyx Geometry, roasted Oct 18), as in test_app.""" c = TestClient(create_app(lake, HeaderAuth())) setup(c) body = {"bag_id": "bag1", "coffee_freetext": "Onyx Geometry", "roast_date": "2026-10-18"} assert c.post("/api/bags", json=body, headers=W).status_code == 200 return c def snapshot(lake, table: str) -> dict: """Every file of a table and its bytes, to show nothing already written was changed or removed.""" return {p.name: p.read_bytes() for p in files(lake, table)} def test_the_bag_page_has_a_finish_button_until_the_bag_is_finished(client): page = client.get("/coffee/bag1").text assert 'data-finish-bag="bag1"' in page and ">Finish bag" in page assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W).status_code == 200 page = client.get("/coffee/bag1").text assert client.get("/coffee/bag1").status_code == 200 assert "data-finish-bag" not in page assert "Roasted Oct 18 · day 12 · finished Oct 30" in page def test_finishing_appends_one_record_and_deletes_nothing(client, lake): client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W) bags_before, shots_before = snapshot(lake, "bags"), snapshot(lake, "shots") r = client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) assert r.json() == {"bag_id": "bag1", "written": True} bags_after = snapshot(lake, "bags") assert {k: v for k, v in bags_after.items() if k in bags_before} == bags_before # untouched new = [lake.root / "bags" / name for name in bags_after.keys() - bags_before.keys()] assert len(new) == 1 (row,) = pq.read_table(new[0]).to_pylist() assert row["bag_id"] == "bag1" and row["finished_on"] == date(2026, 10, 30) and row["deleted"] is False assert (row["coffee_freetext"], row["roast_date"]) == ( "Onyx Geometry", date(2026, 10, 18), ) # the rest kept assert snapshot(lake, "shots") == shots_before # its shots stay as they were # Finishing again (the outbox resending, a second tap) writes nothing. assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W).json()["written"] is False assert len(files(lake, "bags")) == len(bags_after) # A restart reads it back from the lake: still finished, nothing on the grinder. store = create_app(lake, HeaderAuth()).state.store assert store.bag("owner", "bag1").finished_on == date(2026, 10, 30) assert store.current_bag("owner") is None def test_a_finished_bag_leaves_today(client): client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W) client.post("/api/bags", json={"bag_id": "bag2", "coffee_freetext": "Other coffee"}, headers=W) client.get("/bag/bag2/use") today = client.get("/").text assert "Other coffee" in today and "Switch coffee" in today client.post("/api/bags/bag2/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) today = client.get("/").text # the cookie still names bag2 assert "Other coffee" not in today and "/bag/bag2/edit" not in today assert 'href="/coffee/bag1">Onyx Geometry' in today # the open bag is on the grinder again assert "Switch coffee" not in today # one open bag left: nothing to switch to # The last open bag finished: Today no longer offers it as the bag on the grinder. client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) today = client.get("/").text assert "On the grinder" not in today and 'href="/coffee/bag1"' not in today and "Edit bag" not in today assert prefill(client)["bag_id"] is None # Log shot doesn't put a new shot in it def test_a_finished_bag_leaves_the_bag_pickers(client): client.post("/api/bags", json={"bag_id": "bag2", "coffee_freetext": "Other coffee"}, headers=W) client.post("/api/bags", json={"bag_id": "bag3", "coffee_freetext": "Third coffee"}, headers=W) client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1, bag_id="bag3"), headers=W) assert 'href="/bag/bag2/use"' in client.get("/bags/switch").text assert 'href="/log?correct=s1&bag=bag2"' in client.get("/log?correct=s1").text client.post("/api/bags/bag2/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) switch = client.get("/bags/switch").text assert "/bag/bag2/use" not in switch and "Other coffee" not in switch assert 'href="/bag/bag1/use"' in switch and 'href="/bag/bag3/use"' in switch log = client.get("/log?correct=s1").text # the bag list on Log shot when correcting a shot assert "bag=bag2" not in log and 'href="/log?correct=s1&bag=bag1"' in log assert client.get("/bag/bag2/use").status_code == 404 # nor can it be picked by its link def test_a_finished_bag_still_shows_in_coffees(client): client.post("/api/shots", json=shot(1), headers=W) client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W) coffees = client.get("/coffees").text assert 'href="/coffee/bag1"' in coffees and "Onyx Geometry" in coffees assert "1 shot · best rated 4, Oct 21 · finished" in coffees assert "Onyx Geometry" in client.get("/history").text assert client.get("/shot/s1").status_code == 200 def test_finish_is_refused_for_someone_elses_or_a_missing_bag_and_a_bad_date(client, lake): maya = W | {"x-test-user": "maya", "X-Expected-User": "maya"} before = len(files(lake, "bags")) assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH, headers=maya).status_code == 404 assert client.post("/api/bags/nope/finish", json=FINISH, headers=W).status_code == 404 future = (date.today() + timedelta(days=5)).isoformat() assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json={"finished_on": future}, headers=W).status_code == 422 assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json={"finished_on": "soon"}, headers=W).status_code == 422 assert ( client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json=FINISH).status_code == 403 ) # a write needs the app's header assert len(files(lake, "bags")) == before assert client.app.state.store.bag("owner", "bag1").finished_on is None def test_finish_without_a_date_uses_today(client): assert client.post("/api/bags/bag1/finish", json={}, headers=W).json()["written"] is After the review, `git status --short` in the finish-bag worktree shows nothing, and HEAD is still 5eb5cb9. **What the commit contains** (`git show --stat 5eb5cb9`): one commit on `main` (6bda240), touching 6 files with 200 insertions: - a new endpoint, `POST /api/bags/{bag_id}/finish`, in `app/main.py`; - `Store.finish_bag` in `app/store.py`; - the button in `app/templates/coffee.html`; - an outbox handler for `finish:` writes in `app/static/app.js`; - a "Finish bag" section in `docs/app/DESIGN.md`; - `tests/test_finish_bag.py`. The test `test_the_bag_page_has_a_finish_button_until_the_bag_is_finished` passes. - **Writes a record, never deletes:** `finish_bag` commits a copy of the bag with `finished_on` set, under the same id. The test takes a byte-level snapshot and shows the existing bags and shots files are unchanged, with exactly one new parquet row. Finishing an already-finished bag writes nothing. - **Drops it from Today and the Log shot picker:** this commit adds no filtering. The filters (`if not b.finished_on`) were already on `main` in `today`, `switch_bag`, `use_bag`, `log_shot` and `Store.current_bag`/`prefill`, so the commit only adds the write. ## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

- Worktree: /tmp/co-r3/clones/build-finish-bag-screen-with_skill-2-finish-bag (HEAD = 5eb5cb9, clean)

## Verdict

**No blockers.** The change does what the Ask says. It appends one record with `finished_on`, writes no deletes and
leaves existing files untouched. A second finish writes nothing. The button goes away once the bag is finished. The
new tests (7) pass. The findings below are should-fix items and nits.

```

```

---

## Should-fix (minor)

### 1. A finish date before the roast date is accepted, and the page then shows a negative day count. app/store.py:481
`finish_bag` only rejects dates in the future. A phone whose clock reads the past, or any API client, can store a
`finished_on` before `roast_date` or `opened_on`.
```
BEFORE_ROAST: 200 {'bag_id': 'bag1', 'written': True}        # POST {"finished_on": "2025-10-30"}, roast 2026-10-18
PAGE: ['Roasted Oct 18 · day -353 · finished Oct 30']
```
CONFIRMED. The existing Edit bag path doesn't check `finished_on` at all, so this isn't a regression in kind. But the
new code already has a date check, and adding a lower bound there is cheap.

### 2. With no `finished_on` in the body, the server's local date is used, not the user's zone. app/main.py:1030
`date.today()` is the process's local date. The rest of main.py uses `tz(request)` for the viewer's day. The phone
always sends a date, so only API clients are affected.
```
# server TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati, cookie tz=America/Los_Angeles, POST {} on 2026-10-31
NO_DATE: 200 {'bag_id': 'bag1', 'written': True} server date.today()= 2026-11-01
PAGE: ['Roasted Oct 18 · day 14 · finished Nov 1']
```
CONFIRMED. The fix: use `datetime.now(tz(request)).date()`, or require the field.

### 3. Offline, the finished bag stays on the phone's kept Today and Log shot until the write syncs. app/static/app.js:1150 and :107
`clearBagPages()` and clearing `selected-bag` run only inside `deliverOnce` after `r.ok`. Offline, `go(here, ...)`
reloads `/coffee/{id}`, which is in the service worker's KEEP list (app/sw.js:15). That serves the cached copy,
which still has the Finish button and no "finished" date, while the notice says "Bag finished on this phone". The kept
`/` and `/log` still show the bag as current, so shots logged offline get that `bag_id`.
UNPROVEN. This needs a browser with the service worker and a simulated offline state, which I didn't run. The path
is clear from reading the code: app.js:99-115 runs only on `r.ok`, and sw.js:66-68 is the cache fallback. Edit bag's
"Finished" has the same behavior already. DESIGN.md says "Offline it waits in the outbox like any other write", so this
is consistent with the documentation. It is still a gap against "drops it from Today and the bag picker" while offline.

### 4. Read-then-write race with concurrent bag writes. app/store.py:476-483
`prev` is read outside `self.lock`, and `_commit` writes `prev.item.model_copy(...)`. If a concurrent `save_bag` on the
same bag (for example `apply_read` after a photo upload) read the bag before the finish committed, it can write a
later record with `finished_on=None`, and the bag silently reopens. In the other order, the finish copy loses the
photo's `coffee_id`/`match_score`.
UNPROVEN. It's timing-dependent and I wrote no deterministic repro. `save_bag` has the same read-outside-lock
pattern, so this is an existing design limit that the new code inherits, not something it introduced.

## Nits

### 5. A non-string `finished_on` is accepted. app/main.py:1030
`str(body["finished_on"])` makes a JSON number parse as a basic-format ISO date on Python 3.11+.
```
NUMERIC: 200 {'bag_id': 'bag1', 'written': True}             # POST {"finished_on": 20261030}
```
CONFIRMED. A typed Pydantic body model (`finished_on: date | None`) would reject this and match the other endpoints.
A non-dict body is already rejected by FastAPI (`LIST_BODY: 422 {"detail":["Input should be a valid dictionary"]}`),
so that part isn't an issue.

### 6. Duplicated "bag finished" cleanup in `deliverOnce`. app/static/app.js:99-114
The new `finish:` branch sits next to the existing `/api/bags && finished_on` branch and behaves differently. The new
one always clears the kept pages; the existing one clears them only when the finished bag was the selected one. Both
entry bodies carry `bag_id` and `finished_on`, so a single condition would cover both writes.
Proven by reading the diff (shown above in the review session). No runtime repro is needed.

### 7. Duplicated local-date formatter. app/static/app.js:1145
The `YYYY-MM-DD` string built from `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` copies the Edit bag handler (around :698).
Extract a `localToday()` helper. Proven by reading the code: `grep -n 'padStart(2, "0")' app/static/app.js`.

### 8. Duplicated future-date grace rule. app/store.py:481
`datetime.now(UTC).date() + timedelta(days=1)` is copied from `save_bag` (:454), and a comment says it mirrors the
phone's check. Changing one copy and not the other would make the two writes disagree. Proven by reading the code:
`grep -n 'timedelta(days=1)' app/store.py`.

### 9. The test fetches the page twice. tests/test_finish_bag.py:37-38
`page = client.get(...).text` is followed by `assert client.get(...).status_code == 200`, so the status checked isn't
the status of the response whose body is checked. Use `r = client.get(...)` once. Proven by reading the code.

## Scope check against the workstream
- No deletes, and no edits of existing files: covered by `test_finishing_appends_one_record_and_deletes_nothing`.
- Leaves Today and the Log shot picker, stays in Coffees: covered by tests in tests/test_finish_bag.py, all passing.
- No un-finish control and no dbt/model changes. DESIGN.md gains a "Finish bag" section that matches the behavior.
  Nothing is out of scope.

# Code review (medium): finish-bag, main@6bda240..5eb5cb9

- Worktree: /tmp/co-r3/clones/build-finish-bag-screen-with_skill-2-finish-bag (HEAD = 5eb5cb9, clean)
- Context: workstreams/finish-bag.md@52599f1 (orch2 worktree). The Ask: a Finish button on the bag page that writes a
  new record (no deletes), drops the bag from Today and the Log shot picker, keeps it in Coffees, with tests.
- Changed files reviewed: app/main.py, app/store.py, app/static/app.js, app/templates/coffee.html,
  docs/app/DESIGN.md, tests/test_finish_bag.py
- Read-only. No fixes, no push, no PR, no subagents. The /code-review skill ran as a forked execution of this same
  session, not a separate reviewer agent. Repro tests are in /tmp/co-r3/review-scratch/test_review_repro.py,
  outside the worktree.

## Verdict

**No blockers.** The change does what the Ask says. It appends one record with `finished_on`, writes no deletes and
leaves existing files untouched. A second finish writes nothing. The button goes away once the bag is finished. The
new tests (7) pass. The findings below are should-fix items and nits.

### Test suite

```
$ cd <worktree> && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider
FAILED tests/test_verdict.py::test_the_build_takes_claudes_verdict_over_the_rules
1 failed, 564 passed, 83 skipped, 1 warning in 112.96s
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_verdict.py::test_the_build_takes_claudes_verdict_over_the_rules | grep '^E '
E   FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'dbt'
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_finish_bag.py
7 passed in 2.21s
```
The one failure is the environment: `dbt` isn't on PATH, and the test imports none of the changed files. I didn't
run it on `main`, because that would mean creating a worktree, and this review is read-only.

How the repros below were run:
```
cd /tmp/co-r3/clones/build-finish-bag-screen-with_skill-2-finish-bag
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/co-r3/review-scratch/test_review_repro.py -s -q \
  -p no:cacheprovider -p tests.conftest --rootdir=.
```

---

## Should-fix (minor)

### 1. A finish date before the roast date is accepted, and the page then shows a negative day count. app/store.py:481
`finish_bag` only rejects dates in the future. A phone whose clock reads the past, or any API client, can store a
`finished_on` before `roast_date` or `opened_on`.
```
BEFORE_ROAST: 200 {'bag_id': 'bag1', 'written': True}        # POST {"finished_on": "2025-10-30"}, roast 2026-10-18
PAGE: ['Roasted Oct 18 · day -353 · finished Oct 30']
```
CONFIRMED. The existing Edit bag path doesn't check `finished_on` at all, so this isn't a regression in kind. But the
new code already has a date check, and adding a lower bound there is cheap.

### 2. With no `finished_on` in the body, the server's local date is used, not the user's zone. app/main.py:1030
`date.today()` is the process's local date. The rest of main.py uses `tz(request)` for the viewer's day. The phone
always sends a date, so only API clients are affected.
```
# server TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati, cookie tz=America/Los_Angeles, POST {} on 2026-10-31
NO_DATE: 200 {'bag_id': 'bag1', 'written': True} server date.today()= 2026-11-01
PAGE: ['Roasted Oct 18 · day 14 · finished Nov 1']
```
CONFIRMED. The fix: use `datetime.now(tz(request)).date()`, or require the field.

### 3. Offline, the finished bag stays on the phone's kept Today and Log shot until the write syncs. app/static/app.js:1150 and :107
`clearBagPages()` and clearing `selected-bag` run only inside `deliverOnce` after `r.ok`. Offline, `go(here, ...)`
reloads `/coffee/{id}`, which is in the service worker's KEEP list (app/sw.js:15). That serves the cached copy,
which still has the Finish button and no "finished" date, while the notice says "Bag finished on this phone". The kept
`/` and `/log` still show the bag as current, so shots logged offline get that `bag_id`.
UNPROVEN. This needs a browser with the service worker and a simulated offline state, which I didn't run. The path
is clear from reading the code: app.js:99-115 runs only on `r.ok`, and sw.js:66-68 is the cache fallback. Edit bag's
"Finished" has the same behavior already. DESIGN.md says "Offline it waits in the outbox like any other write", so this
is consistent with the documentation. It is still a gap against "drops it from Today and the bag picker" while offline.

### 4. Read-then-write race with concurrent bag writes. app/store.py:476-483
`prev` is read outside `self.lock`, and `_commit` writes `prev.item.model_copy(...)`. If a concurrent `save_bag` on the
same bag (for example `apply_read` after a photo upload) read the bag before the finish committed, it can write a
later record with `finished_on=None`, and the bag silently reopens. In the other order, the finish copy loses the
photo's `coffee_id`/`match_score`.
UNPROVEN. It's timing-dependent and I wrote no deterministic repro. `save_bag` has the same read-outside-lock
pattern, so this is an existing design limit that the new code inherits, not something it introduced.

## Nits

### 5. A non-string `finished_on` is accepted. app/main.py:1030
`str(body["finished_on"])` makes a JSON number parse as a basic-format ISO date on Python 3.11+.
```
NUMERIC: 200 {'bag_id': 'bag1', 'written': True}             # POST {"finished_on": 20261030}
```
CONFIRMED. A typed Pydantic body model (`finished_on: date | None`) would reject this and match the other endpoints.
A non-dict body is already rejected by FastAPI (`LIST_BODY: 422 {"detail":["Input should be a valid dictionary"]}`),
so that part isn't an issue.

### 6. Duplicated "bag finished" cleanup in `deliverOnce`. app/static/app.js:99-114
The new `finish:` branch sits next to the existing `/api/bags && finished_on` branch and behaves differently. The new
one always clears the kept pages; the existing one clears them only when the finished bag was the selected one. Both
entry bodies carry `bag_id` and `finished_on`, so a single condition would cover both writes.
Proven by reading the diff (shown above in the review session). No runtime repro is needed.

### 7. Duplicated local-date formatter. app/static/app.js:1145
The `YYYY-MM-DD` string built from `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` copies the Edit bag handler (around :698).
Extract a `localToday()` helper. Proven by reading the code: `grep -n 'padStart(2, "0")' app/static/app.js`.

### 8. Duplicated future-date grace rule. app/store.py:481
`datetime.now(UTC).date() + timedelta(days=1)` is copied from `save_bag` (:454), and a comment says it mirrors the
phone's check. Changing one copy and not the other would make the two writes disagree. Proven by reading the code:
`grep -n 'timedelta(days=1)' app/store.py`.

### 9. The test fetches the page twice. tests/test_finish_bag.py:37-38
`page = client.get(...).text` is followed by `assert client.get(...).status_code == 200`, so the status checked isn't
the status of the response whose body is checked. Use `r = client.get(...)` once. Proven by reading the code.

## Scope check against the workstream
- No deletes, and no edits of existing files: covered by `test_finishing_appends_one_record_and_deletes_nothing`.
- Leaves Today and the Log shot picker, stays in Coffees: covered by tests in tests/test_finish_bag.py, all passing.
- No un-finish control and no dbt/model changes. DESIGN.md gains a "Finish bag" section that matches the behavior.
  Nothing is out of scope.
